# Log panic message before aborting

## Pull Request by @tomusdrw

## Summary
- `panic()` now calls the `log` ecalli at Fatal level (target: `"panic"`) before calling `abort()`, so the message is visible in host logs even when the abort trap doesn't surface it.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run build` passes (all examples compile and PVM-compile)
- [x] `npm test` passes (153 tests across SDK and examples)
- [x] `npx biome ci` passes

## Walkthrough

The `panic` function in `sdk/core/panic.ts` now logs a structured entry before terminating execution. The implementation imports a `log` module and, when invoked, encodes the string `"panic"` and the provided `msg` parameter as UTF-8 buffers. Their byte lengths and pointers (cast via `changetype<u32>`) are passed to `log(0, ...)`. Following the log operation, execution terminates via `abort(msg)`. The function signature remains unchanged. Six lines of code were added.

## Comment by @coderabbitai[bot]

_🧹 Nitpick_ | _🔵 Trivial_

**Consider explicit casts for `byteLength` to `u32`.**

The `log` ecalli expects `u32` for length parameters, but `ArrayBuffer.byteLength` returns `i32` in AssemblyScript. While implicit conversion works for non-negative lengths, explicit casts would ensure type consistency with the function signature.



<details>
<summary>♻️ Suggested change</summary>

```diff
   const target = "panic";
   const targetBuf = String.UTF8.encode(target);
   const msgBuf = String.UTF8.encode(msg);
-  log(0, changetype<u32>(targetBuf), targetBuf.byteLength, changetype<u32>(msgBuf), msgBuf.byteLength);
+  log(0, changetype<u32>(targetBuf), u32(targetBuf.byteLength), changetype<u32>(msgBuf), u32(msgBuf.byteLength));
```
</details>
